title: Your Body Language May Shape Who You Are | Amy Cuddy | TED
speaker: TED

cues.text: Translator: Joseph Geni Reviewer: Morton Bast
cues.en: Translator: Joseph Geni Reviewer: Morton Bast
cues.zh: 譯者：Joseph Geni 審稿者：Morton Bast

cues.text: So I want to start by offering you a free no-tech life hack,
cues.en: So I want to start by offering you a free no-tech life hack,
cues.zh: 所以我想先為您提供免費的無科技生活小技巧，

cues.text: and all it requires of you is this: that you change your posture for two minutes.
cues.en: and all it requires of you is this: that you change your posture for two minutes.
cues.zh: 它對你的要求就是：改變姿勢兩分鐘。

cues.text: But before I give it away, I want to ask you to right now do a little audit of your body and what you're doing with your body.
cues.en: But before I give it away, I want to ask you to right now do a little audit of your body and what you're doing with your body.
cues.zh: 但在我透露之前，我想請您現在對您的身體以及您對身體所做的事情進行一些檢查。

cues.text: So how many of you are sort of making yourselves smaller?
cues.en: So how many of you are sort of making yourselves smaller?
cues.zh: 那麼，你們當中有多少人在某種程度上讓自己變得更小呢？

cues.text: Maybe you're hunching, crossing your legs, maybe wrapping your ankles.
cues.en: Maybe you're hunching, crossing your legs, maybe wrapping your ankles.
cues.zh: 也許你彎腰駝背，交叉雙腿，也許包裹腳踝。

cues.text: Sometimes we hold onto our arms like this.
cues.en: Sometimes we hold onto our arms like this.
cues.zh: 有時我們會這樣握住手臂。

cues.text: Sometimes we spread out.
cues.en: Sometimes we spread out.
cues.zh: 有時我們會分散開來。

cues.text: I see you.
cues.en: I see you.
cues.zh: 我看見你。

cues.text: So I want you to pay attention to what you're doing right now.
cues.en: So I want you to pay attention to what you're doing right now.
cues.zh: 所以我希望你注意你現在正在做的事情。

cues.text: We're going to come back to that in a few minutes, and I'm hoping that if you learn to tweak this a little bit,
cues.en: We're going to come back to that in a few minutes, and I'm hoping that if you learn to tweak this a little bit,
cues.zh: 我們將在幾分鐘後回到這個問題，我希望如果你學會稍微調整一下，

cues.text: it could significantly change the way your life unfolds.
cues.en: it could significantly change the way your life unfolds.
cues.zh: 它可以顯著改變你的生活方式。

cues.text: So, we're really fascinated with body language, and we're particularly interested in other people's body language.
cues.en: So, we're really fascinated with body language, and we're particularly interested in other people's body language.
cues.zh: 所以，我們真的對肢體語言著迷，對其他人的肢體語言特別感興趣。

cues.text: You know, we're interested in, like, you know —
cues.en: You know, we're interested in, like, you know —
cues.zh: 你知道，我們感興趣的是，你知道——

cues.text: an awkward interaction, or a smile, or a contemptuous glance, or maybe a very awkward wink,
cues.en: an awkward interaction, or a smile, or a contemptuous glance, or maybe a very awkward wink,
cues.zh: 尷尬的互動，或是微笑，或是輕蔑的眼神，或者可能是一個非常尷尬的眨眼，

cues.text: or maybe even something like a handshake.
cues.en: or maybe even something like a handshake.
cues.zh: 或甚至是握手之類的東西。

cues.text: Narrator: Here they are arriving at Number 10.
cues.en: Narrator: Here they are arriving at Number 10.
cues.zh: 旁白：他們來到了10號。

cues.text: This lucky policeman gets to shake hands with the President of the United States.
cues.en: This lucky policeman gets to shake hands with the President of the United States.
cues.zh: 這位幸運的警察能夠與美國總統握手。

cues.text: Here comes the Prime Minister -- No.
cues.en: Here comes the Prime Minister -- No.
cues.zh: 首相來了——不。

cues.text: Amy Cuddy: So a handshake, or the lack of a handshake,
cues.en: Amy Cuddy: So a handshake, or the lack of a handshake,
cues.zh: 艾米·卡迪：所以握手，或不握手，

cues.text: can have us talking for weeks and weeks and weeks.
cues.en: can have us talking for weeks and weeks and weeks.
cues.zh: 可以讓我們談談數週、數週、數週。

cues.text: Even the BBC and The New York Times.
cues.en: Even the BBC and The New York Times.
cues.zh: 甚至 BBC 和紐約時報。

cues.text: So obviously when we think about nonverbal behavior,
cues.en: So obviously when we think about nonverbal behavior,
cues.zh: 顯然，當我們考慮非語言行為時，

cues.text: or body language -- but we call it nonverbals as social scientists -- it's language, so we think about communication.
cues.en: or body language -- but we call it nonverbals as social scientists -- it's language, so we think about communication.
cues.zh: 或肢體語言——但我們作為社會科學家稱之為非語言——它是語言，所以我們考慮溝通。

cues.text: When we think about communication, we think about interactions.
cues.en: When we think about communication, we think about interactions.
cues.zh: 當我們考慮溝通時，我們會考慮互動。

cues.text: So what is your body language communicating to me?
cues.en: So what is your body language communicating to me?
cues.zh: 那麼你的肢體語言在傳達什麼訊息給我呢？

cues.text: What's mine communicating to you?
cues.en: What's mine communicating to you?
cues.zh: 我在跟你傳達什麼訊息？

cues.text: And there's a lot of reason to believe that this is a valid way to look at this.
cues.en: And there's a lot of reason to believe that this is a valid way to look at this.
cues.zh: 有很多理由相信這是看待這個問題的有效方法。

cues.text: So social scientists have spent a lot of time looking at the effects of our body language,
cues.en: So social scientists have spent a lot of time looking at the effects of our body language,
cues.zh: 所以社會科學家花了很多時間研究我們肢體語言的影響，

cues.text: or other people's body language, on judgments.
cues.en: or other people's body language, on judgments.
cues.zh: 或是其他人的肢體語言，來進行判斷。

cues.text: And we make sweeping judgments and inferences from body language.
cues.en: And we make sweeping judgments and inferences from body language.
cues.zh: 我們根據肢體語言做出全面的判斷和推論。

cues.text: And those judgments can predict really meaningful life outcomes
cues.en: And those judgments can predict really meaningful life outcomes
cues.zh: 這些判斷可以預測真正有意義的生活結果

cues.text: like who we hire or promote, who we ask out on a date.
cues.en: like who we hire or promote, who we ask out on a date.
cues.zh: 例如我們僱用或提拔誰，我們約誰出去約會。

cues.text: For example, Nalini Ambady, a researcher at Tufts University,
cues.en: For example, Nalini Ambady, a researcher at Tufts University,
cues.zh: 例如，塔夫茨大學研究員 Nalini Ambady，

cues.text: shows that when people watch 30-second soundless clips
cues.en: shows that when people watch 30-second soundless clips
cues.zh: 表示當人們觀看 30 秒的無聲片段時

cues.text: of real physician-patient interactions, their judgments of the physician's niceness
cues.en: of real physician-patient interactions, their judgments of the physician's niceness
cues.zh: 真實的醫病互動，他們對醫生友善的判斷

cues.text: predict whether or not that physician will be sued.
cues.en: predict whether or not that physician will be sued.
cues.zh: 預測該醫生是否會被起訴。

cues.text: So it doesn't have to do so much with whether or not that physician was incompetent,
cues.en: So it doesn't have to do so much with whether or not that physician was incompetent,
cues.zh: 所以這與醫生是否無能沒有太大關係

cues.text: but do we like that person and how they interacted?
cues.en: but do we like that person and how they interacted?
cues.zh: 但我們喜歡那個人以及他們的互動方式嗎？

cues.text: Even more dramatic, Alex Todorov at Princeton has shown us that judgments of political candidates' faces
cues.en: Even more dramatic, Alex Todorov at Princeton has shown us that judgments of political candidates' faces
cues.zh: 更戲劇性的是，普林斯頓大學的亞歷克斯·託多羅夫（Alex Todorov）向我們展示了對政治候選人面孔的判斷

cues.text: in just one second predict 70 percent of U.S. Senate and gubernatorial race outcomes,
cues.en: in just one second predict 70 percent of U.S. Senate and gubernatorial race outcomes,
cues.zh: 只需一秒鐘即可預測 70% 的美國參議院和州長競選結果，

cues.text: and even, let's go digital, emoticons used well in online negotiations
cues.en: and even, let's go digital, emoticons used well in online negotiations
cues.zh: 甚至，讓我們走向數位化，線上上談判中使用得很好的表情符號

cues.text: can lead you to claim more value from that negotiation.
cues.en: can lead you to claim more value from that negotiation.
cues.zh: 可以引導您從談判中獲得更多價值。

cues.text: If you use them poorly, bad idea. Right?
cues.en: If you use them poorly, bad idea. Right?
cues.zh: 如果你使用不當，那是個壞主意。正確的？

cues.text: So when we think of nonverbals, we think of how we judge others, how they judge us and what the outcomes are.
cues.en: So when we think of nonverbals, we think of how we judge others, how they judge us and what the outcomes are.
cues.zh: 因此，當我們想到非語言時，我們會想到我們如何評價他人，他們如何評價我們以及結果是什麼。

cues.text: We tend to forget, though, the other audience that's influenced by our nonverbals, and that's ourselves.
cues.en: We tend to forget, though, the other audience that's influenced by our nonverbals, and that's ourselves.
cues.zh: 然而，我們往往會忘記受我們的非語言影響的其他觀眾，那就是我們自己。

cues.text: We are also influenced by our nonverbals, our thoughts and our feelings and our physiology.
cues.en: We are also influenced by our nonverbals, our thoughts and our feelings and our physiology.
cues.zh: 我們也受到我們的非語言、我們的思想、我們的感受和我們的生理的影響。

cues.text: So what nonverbals am I talking about?
cues.en: So what nonverbals am I talking about?
cues.zh: 那我在談論什麼非語言呢？

cues.text: I'm a social psychologist. I study prejudice, and I teach at a competitive business school,
cues.en: I'm a social psychologist. I study prejudice, and I teach at a competitive business school,
cues.zh: 我是一名社會心理學家。我研究偏見，在一所競爭激烈的商學院任教，

cues.text: so it was inevitable that I would become interested in power dynamics.
cues.en: so it was inevitable that I would become interested in power dynamics.
cues.zh: 所以我不可避免地會對權力動力學產生興趣。

cues.text: I became especially interested in nonverbal expressions of power and dominance.
cues.en: I became especially interested in nonverbal expressions of power and dominance.
cues.zh: 我對權力和統治力的非語言表達特別感興趣。

cues.text: And what are nonverbal expressions of power and dominance?
cues.en: And what are nonverbal expressions of power and dominance?
cues.zh: 什麼是權力和統治力的非語言表達？

cues.text: Well, this is what they are.
cues.en: Well, this is what they are.
cues.zh: 嗯，這就是他們的本質。

cues.text: So in the animal kingdom, they are about expanding.
cues.en: So in the animal kingdom, they are about expanding.
cues.zh: 所以在動物王國裡，它們正在擴張。

cues.text: So you make yourself big, you stretch out, you take up space, you're basically opening up.
cues.en: So you make yourself big, you stretch out, you take up space, you're basically opening up.
cues.zh: 所以你讓自己變得更大，你伸展，你佔據空間，你基本上是在開放。

cues.text: It's about opening up.
cues.en: It's about opening up.
cues.zh: 這是關於開放。

cues.text: And this is true across the animal kingdom.
cues.en: And this is true across the animal kingdom.
cues.zh: 在整個動物王國都是如此。

cues.text: It's not just limited to primates.
cues.en: It's not just limited to primates.
cues.zh: 它不僅限於靈長類動物。

cues.text: And humans do the same thing.
cues.en: And humans do the same thing.
cues.zh: 人類也做同樣的事情。

cues.text: So they do this both when they have power sort of chronically,
cues.en: So they do this both when they have power sort of chronically,
cues.zh: 因此，當他們長期擁有權力時，他們都會這樣做，

cues.text: and also when they're feeling powerful in the moment.
cues.en: and also when they're feeling powerful in the moment.
cues.zh: 當他們此刻感覺強大時也是如此。

cues.text: And this one is especially interesting because it really shows us how universal and old these expressions of power are.
cues.en: And this one is especially interesting because it really shows us how universal and old these expressions of power are.
cues.zh: 這一點特別有趣，因為它確實向我們展示了這些權力表達方式是多麼普遍和古老。

cues.text: This expression, which is known as pride, Jessica Tracy has studied.
cues.en: This expression, which is known as pride, Jessica Tracy has studied.
cues.zh: 傑西卡·特蕾西研究過這種被稱為驕傲的表達方式。

cues.text: She shows that people who are born with sight and people who are congenitally blind do this
cues.en: She shows that people who are born with sight and people who are congenitally blind do this
cues.zh: 她表明，天生有視力的人和先天失明的人都會這樣做

cues.text: when they win at a physical competition.
cues.en: when they win at a physical competition.
cues.zh: 當他們在體育比賽中獲勝時。

cues.text: So when they cross the finish line and they've won, it doesn't matter if they've never seen anyone do it.
cues.en: So when they cross the finish line and they've won, it doesn't matter if they've never seen anyone do it.
cues.zh: 因此，當他們衝過終點線並獲勝時，即使他們從未見過有人這樣做也沒關係。

cues.text: They do this.
cues.en: They do this.
cues.zh: 他們這樣做。

cues.text: So the arms up in the V, the chin is slightly lifted.
cues.en: So the arms up in the V, the chin is slightly lifted.
cues.zh: 所以雙臂向上呈V字形，下巴微微抬起。

cues.text: What do we do when we feel powerless?
cues.en: What do we do when we feel powerless?
cues.zh: 當我們感到無能為力時，我們該怎麼辦？

cues.text: We do exactly the opposite.
cues.en: We do exactly the opposite.
cues.zh: 我們的做法恰恰相反。

cues.text: We close up. We wrap ourselves up.
cues.en: We close up. We wrap ourselves up.
cues.zh: 我們關閉。我們把自己包裹起來。

cues.text: We make ourselves small.
cues.en: We make ourselves small.
cues.zh: 我們讓自己變得渺小。

cues.text: We don't want to bump into the person next to us.
cues.en: We don't want to bump into the person next to us.
cues.zh: 我們不想撞到旁邊的人。

cues.text: So again, both animals and humans do the same thing.
cues.en: So again, both animals and humans do the same thing.
cues.zh: 同樣，動物和人類都做同樣的事情。

cues.text: And this is what happens when you put together high and low power.
cues.en: And this is what happens when you put together high and low power.
cues.zh: 這就是當你將高功率和低功率放在一起時會發生的情況。

cues.text: So what we tend to do when it comes to power is that we complement the other's nonverbals.
cues.en: So what we tend to do when it comes to power is that we complement the other's nonverbals.
cues.zh: 因此，當涉及到權力時，我們傾向於做的就是補充對方的非語言能力。

cues.text: So if someone is being really powerful with us, we tend to make ourselves smaller. We don't mirror them.
cues.en: So if someone is being really powerful with us, we tend to make ourselves smaller. We don't mirror them.
cues.zh: 因此，如果有人對我們非常強大，我們會傾向於讓自己變得更渺小。我們不映象他們。

cues.text: We do the opposite of them.
cues.en: We do the opposite of them.
cues.zh: 我們做的與他們相反。

cues.text: So I'm watching this behavior in the classroom, and what do I notice?
cues.en: So I'm watching this behavior in the classroom, and what do I notice?
cues.zh: 那麼我在教室裡觀察這種行為，我注意到了什麼？

cues.text: I notice that MBA students really exhibit the full range of power nonverbals.
cues.en: I notice that MBA students really exhibit the full range of power nonverbals.
cues.zh: 我注意到 MBA 學生確實展現了全方位的非語言能力。

cues.text: So you have people who are like caricatures of alphas, really coming into the room, they get right into the middle of the room
cues.en: So you have people who are like caricatures of alphas, really coming into the room, they get right into the middle of the room
cues.zh: 所以有人就像漫畫中的阿爾法，真正進入房間，直接進入房間的中間

cues.text: before class even starts, like they really want to occupy space.
cues.en: before class even starts, like they really want to occupy space.
cues.zh: 甚至在上課之前，他們就好像真的想佔據空間一樣。

cues.text: When they sit down, they're sort of spread out.
cues.en: When they sit down, they're sort of spread out.
cues.zh: 當他們坐下時，他們會分散開來。

cues.text: They raise their hands like this.
cues.en: They raise their hands like this.
cues.zh: 他們像這樣舉起手來。

cues.text: You have other people who are virtually collapsing when they come in. As soon they come in, you see it.
cues.en: You have other people who are virtually collapsing when they come in. As soon they come in, you see it.
cues.zh: 還有一些人進來時幾乎崩潰了。他們一進來，你就看到了。

cues.text: You see it on their faces and their bodies, and they sit in their chair and they make themselves tiny,
cues.en: You see it on their faces and their bodies, and they sit in their chair and they make themselves tiny,
cues.zh: 你可以在他們的臉上和身體上看到這一點，他們坐在椅子上，讓自己變得很小，

cues.text: and they go like this when they raise their hand.
cues.en: and they go like this when they raise their hand.
cues.zh: 當他們舉手時，他們就會這樣走。

cues.text: I notice a couple of things about this.
cues.en: I notice a couple of things about this.
cues.zh: 我注意到有關於此的一些事情。

cues.text: One, you're not going to be surprised.
cues.en: One, you're not going to be surprised.
cues.zh: 第一，你不會感到驚訝。

cues.text: It seems to be related to gender.
cues.en: It seems to be related to gender.
cues.zh: 這似乎與性別有關。

cues.text: So women are much more likely to do this kind of thing than men.
cues.en: So women are much more likely to do this kind of thing than men.
cues.zh: 所以女性比男性更容易做這種事。

cues.text: Women feel chronically less powerful than men, so this is not surprising.
cues.en: Women feel chronically less powerful than men, so this is not surprising.
cues.zh: 女性長期感覺不如男性強大，所以這並不奇怪。

cues.text: But the other thing I noticed is that it also seemed to be related to the extent
cues.en: But the other thing I noticed is that it also seemed to be related to the extent
cues.zh: 但我注意到的另一件事是，它似乎也與程度有關

cues.text: to which the students were participating, and how well they were participating.
cues.en: to which the students were participating, and how well they were participating.
cues.zh: 學生參與的內容以及他們的參與程度。

cues.text: And this is really important in the MBA classroom, because participation counts for half the grade.
cues.en: And this is really important in the MBA classroom, because participation counts for half the grade.
cues.zh: 這在 MBA 課堂上非常重要，因為參與度佔成績的一半。

cues.text: So business schools have been struggling with this gender grade gap.
cues.en: So business schools have been struggling with this gender grade gap.
cues.zh: 因此，商學院一直在努力解決這種性別成績差距。

cues.text: You get these equally qualified women and men coming in and then you get these differences in grades,
cues.en: You get these equally qualified women and men coming in and then you get these differences in grades,
cues.zh: 你讓這些同等資格的女性和男性進來，然後你會發現成績上的差異，

cues.text: and it seems to be partly attributable to participation.
cues.en: and it seems to be partly attributable to participation.
cues.zh: 這似乎部分歸因於參與。

cues.text: So I started to wonder, you know, okay, so you have these people coming in like this, and they're participating.
cues.en: So I started to wonder, you know, okay, so you have these people coming in like this, and they're participating.
cues.zh: 所以我開始想，你知道，好吧，所以這些人就像這樣進來，他們正在參與。

cues.text: Is it possible that we could get people to fake it and would it lead them to participate more?
cues.en: Is it possible that we could get people to fake it and would it lead them to participate more?
cues.zh: 我們是否有可能讓人們偽造它並會導致他們更多地參與？

cues.text: So my main collaborator Dana Carney, who's at Berkeley,
cues.en: So my main collaborator Dana Carney, who's at Berkeley,
cues.zh: 我的主要合作者達納卡尼 (Dana Carney) 在柏克萊分校

cues.text: and I really wanted to know, can you fake it till you make it?
cues.en: and I really wanted to know, can you fake it till you make it?
cues.zh: 我真的很想知道，你能假裝它直到你成功嗎？

cues.en: and also I want to ask you to share the science, because this is simple.
cues.zh: 我也想請您分享科學原理，因為這很簡單。

cues.zh: 把它丟掉。與人分享，因為最能使用它的人

cues.zh: 把它交給他們，因為他們可以私下做。
